target.title: fix(memory): skip blank search provider bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search handled blank or whitespace-only queries too late. The manager could initialize the provider, assert provider state, or bootstrap search work before the preflight returned an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blank query eligibility is a local preflight contract and should not require provider setup. This change shares query normalization with the existing preflight and short-circuits blank queries before provider/bootstrap work.

## User Impact

Whitespace-only memory searches return `[]` cheaply and deterministically, without requiring provider credentials, indexes, or search startup.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`.
- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.ts`.
- Added `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts` proving blank search returns `[]` before provider init, provider assertion, index check, or sync bootstrap.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Controlled manager proof: `node --import tsx - <<'EOF' ...` invoked the actual `MemoryIndexManager.search` method with a whitespace-only query and provider/bootstrap counters.
- Normal manager proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF' ...` constructed a real `MemoryIndexManager` through `MemoryIndexManager.get({ cfg, agentId: "main", purpose: "cli" })`, then ran a whitespace-only search.

## Proof

- Controlled proof query: whitespace-only.
- Controlled proof result: `resultCount: 0`, `results: []`.
- Provider/bootstrap counters all stayed zero: `ensureProviderInitialized: 0`, `assertRequiredProviderAvailable: 0`, `hasIndexedContent: 0`, `sync: 0`.
- Normal manager proof used a temporary workspace/state dir and `provider: "none"` with vector disabled to avoid external provider setup.
- Normal manager proof output:
  - `managerConstructed: true`
  - `purpose: "cli"`
  - `blankResultCount: 0`, `blankResults: []`
  - `beforeProviderState` and `afterProviderState`: `{ "mode": "pending", "requestedProvider": "none" }`
  - `beforeFiles: 0`, `afterFiles: 0`, `beforeChunks: 0`, `afterChunks: 0`
- This proves the blank-query preflight returns before provider initialization, provider availability assertion, index checks, or sync bootstrap on both the direct search method and a normally constructed manager path.


## Public CLI Proof

- Public CLI proof command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`, with `<whitespace>` equal to `" \n\t "` in a temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and workspace.
- Config used `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "none"`, `store.vector.enabled: false`, and search/index watchers disabled, so a blank-query preflight must not need any embedding provider.
- Search exit: `0`.
- Search stdout:
  ```json
  {
    "results": []
  }
  ```
- Follow-up status command: `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` in the same fixture.
- Follow-up status core: `provider: "none"`, `requestedProvider: "none"`, `vector.enabled: false`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, `dirty: true`.
- Workspace contents stayed `MEMORY.md` plus `memory/`; only the normal OpenClaw state SQLite files were created under the temporary state dir.
- This proves the public `openclaw memory search` path returns `[]` for a whitespace-only query before provider/bootstrap/index work.

## Required Provider CLI Comparison
Current-main baseline: `upstream/main@fab69517b3`. PR head: `a7cc3fc2096915f8956c529193bb32d4e6c30bbe`.

I ran the same public CLI command against current main and this PR head with an explicit required remote provider and intentionally absent credentials:

- Command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`
- Environment: `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`
- Config: `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "openai"`, `model: "text-embedding-3-small"`, `fallback: "none"`, `sync.watch/onSessionStart/onSearch: false`, `store.vector.enabled: true`

Redacted output:

```text
upstream/main@fab69517b3
exitCode: 1
stderr: Memory search failed: No API key found for provider "openai" ... | missing-provider-auth
stdout: [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.

PR head@a7cc3fc209
exitCode: 0
stdout: {
  "results": []
}
stderr: $ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search --query '<whitespace>' --json
```

The same fixture's `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` output on both revisions reported `provider: "openai"`, `requestedProvider: "openai"`, `vector.enabled: true`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, and `providerState.mode: "pending"`. That confirms this is not `provider: "none"` FTS-only proof: current main reaches required-provider auth before blank-query rejection, while the patched head returns the blank-query `[]` result before provider/bootstrap/index work.
